disability-advocates-and-caregivers-holi.headline: Disability Advocates & Caregivers - Holiday Grocery Accessibility
disability-advocates-and-caregivers-holi.author: Aaron Di Blasi, PMP
disability-advocates-and-caregivers-holi.core: Posted in last 7 days Disability Advocates & Caregivers - Holiday Grocery Accessibility 🎙️ Remarkable World Commentary Episode #125: Ask Advocate Donna | By Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA | Courtesy of the PWD Media Co-op https://lnkd.in/ePFyHXQN In this thought-provoking episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan presents her second solo podcast for the month of November, an Ask Advocate Donna session, thanking listeners for their comments and feedback and inviting them to keep writing to [email redacted]. She opens with a famous quote by an unknown author, "Speak in such a way that others would love to listen to you, and listen in such a way that others would love to speak to you," and then plays her monthly word game, asking advocates to think about two pairs of words, remembering or forgetting, and ready or running away, where being ready means pushing off from the starting blocks and running away means turning and leaving the track because you just don't think you can deal with something. Donna then shares three stories of the month sent in by listeners, asking of each what advocacy is, who gets involved, why it is necessary, and how and when to get involved. In the first, Danielle and her vision-impaired daughter, Greta, were offered one box of food to share at a Christmastime function, and the hostess handed over a second box only after Danielle objected and Greta spoke up for herself. In the second, Mary could not access the QR code mailed to her for the census, and Donna says she would seek a toll-free number rather than depend on sighted assistance, though even that is not equal access because it is a workaround. In the third, Sean, a senior with some physical challenges, asked three times at the checkout of a Walmart store in Scarborough, Ontario for help packing his groceries and was ignored; Donna recalls leaving everything and walking away when she was refused help many years ago, and says Sean should start the ball rolling by reporting the incident to Walmart's customer service department. Calling November the busy month before the holiday season, she says she thinks the third story was chosen because of the oncoming holiday season, and thanks listeners for tuning in.
